source.primary_witnesses: MT BHS Codex Leningradensis — entirely Aramaic. The lions' den narrative. SECONDARY: 4Q112 (Daniela) + 4Q116 preserve fragments; the DSS witness confirms the MT outline. TERTIARY: OG presents a substantially divergent narrative arc (Darius's role differs, the conspirators are explicitly named as two satraps, the lions are starved differently); Theodotion-Greek conforms more closely to MT. The historical 'Darius the Mede' (v 1) is not directly attested in cuneiform sources — proposals include Gubaru/Ugbaru (governor of Babylon under Cyrus), Cyrus himself ('Darius' being a throne-name), or Cyaxares II per Xenophon Cyropaedia (but Cyaxares II is widely regarded as a Xenophontic literary creation).
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against BHS apparatus + DJD XVI 2000 + Ziegler-Munnich 1999.
source.fetchedFrom: BHS; Ulrich DJD XVI 2000; Collins 1993 Hermeneia; Goldingay 1989 WBC; Newsom 2014 OTL; Montgomery 1927 ICC; Ziegler-Munnich 1999.
source.citation: BHS (Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft 1997); Ulrich et al. 2000 DJD XVI; Collins 1993 Hermeneia; Goldingay 1989 WBC; Newsom 2014 OTL; Montgomery 1927 ICC; Ziegler-Munnich 1999 Septuaginta XVI.2.
source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 6 — ARAMAIC, the lions' den + the prayer-prohibition decree. **VERSE NUMBERING**: BHS 6:1 = English 5:31 ('Darius the Mede received the kingdom...'); BHS 6:2-29 = English 6:1-28. This file follows BHS numbering: 28 verses. The chapter is a structural twin of ch 3 (the fiery furnace): a Persian-period martyrology of the loyal-Jew-vs-pagan-court-conspiracy type. The 'irrevocable law of the Medes and Persians' (vv 8, 12, 15) is a literary trope (no cuneiform evidence for absolute-irrevocability of Persian royal decrees; Persian royal practice did allow amendment). Daniel's rescue by an angel (v 22) mirrors the fourth-man rescue in 3:25, 28.

verses.text: וְדָרְיָ֙וֶשׁ֙ מָֽדָאָ֔ה קַבֵּ֖ל מַלְכוּתָ֑א כְּבַ֥ר שְׁנִ֖ין שִׁתִּ֥ין וְתַרְתֵּֽין׃
verses.translit: wə-Dāryāweš Māḏāʾāh qabbēl malḵūṯāʾ kə-ḇar šənîn šittîn wə-ṯartên
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:1 (= English 5:31; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Darius the Mede received the kingdom, being about sixty-two years old.** **VERSE NUMBERING**: BHS 6:1 = English 5:31. **HISTORICAL CRUX**: 'Darius the Mede' (דָרְיָוֶשׁ מָדָאָה) is not directly attested in cuneiform. Cyrus took Babylon 539 BCE. Three main scholarly proposals: (a) Gubaru/Ugbaru, the general who took Babylon, briefly governed and died within weeks per Nabonidus Chronicle iii.22-24; (b) the figure is a confused conflation of Darius I (522-486) with the Median conquest of Babylon; (c) Cyrus himself, 'Darius' being a throne-name (Wiseman 1965). Collins 1993 + Newsom 2014: literary-theological figure, not strictly historical.

verses.text: שְׁפַר֙ קֳדָ֣ם דָּרְיָ֔וֶשׁ וַהֲקִים֙ עַל־מַלְכוּתָ֔א לַאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֖א מְאָ֣ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֑ין דִּ֥י לֶהֱוֹ֖ן בְּכָל־מַלְכוּתָֽא׃
verses.translit: šəp̄ar qŏdām Dāryāweš wa-hăqîm ʿal-malḵūṯāʾ la-ʾăḥašdarpənayyāʾ məʾāh wə-ʿeśrîn dī lehĕwōn bə-ḵol-malḵūṯāʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:2 (= English 6:1; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **It pleased Darius to set over the kingdom one hundred and twenty satraps, to be throughout the whole kingdom.** **NUMBER**: 120 satraps is higher than the cuneiform-attested 20-28 satrapies of Darius I (per Herodotus 3.89); the Daniel number may be schematic (120 = 12 × 10). The number 127 appears in Esth 1:1 + 8:9 for Ahasuerus's satrapies — close but distinct. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Acts 1:15 (the 120 disciples in Jerusalem) — possibly Lucan allusion to Dan 6:2.

verses.text: וְעֵ֤לָּא מִנְּהוֹן֙ סָרְכִ֣ין תְּלָתָ֔א דִּ֥י דָנִיֵּ֖אל חַֽד־מִנְּה֑וֹן דִּֽי־לֶהֱוֹ֞ן אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֗ין יָהֲבִ֤ין לְהוֹן֙ טַעְמָ֔א וּמַלְכָּ֖א לָֽא־לֶהֱוֵ֥א נָזִֽק׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿēllāʾ minnəhōn sārəḵîn təlāṯāʾ dī Dāniyyēʾl ḥaḏ-minnəhōn dî-lehĕwōn ʾăḥašdarpənayyāʾ ʾillên yāhăḇîn lə-hōn ṭaʿmāʾ ū-malkāʾ lāʾ-lehĕwēʾ nāziq
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:3 (= English 6:2; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Over them three presidents, of whom Daniel was one; the satraps should give account to them, that the king might suffer no loss.** **TERM**: סָרְכִין (sārəḵîn 'high officials, presidents') — Persian loanword *sraka-*. Daniel as one of three top-tier administrators sets up the conspiracy motive.

verses.text: אֱדַ֙יִן֙ דָּנִיֵּ֣אל דְּנָ֔ה הֲוָ֣א מִתְנַצַּ֔ח עַל־סָרְכַיָּ֖א וַאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֑א כָּל־קֳבֵ֗ל דִּ֣י ר֤וּחַ יַתִּירָא֙ בֵּ֔הּ וּמַלְכָּ֣א עֲשִׁ֔ית לַהֲקָמוּתֵ֖הּ עַל־כָּל־מַלְכוּתָֽא׃
verses.translit: ʾĕdayin Dāniyyēʾl dənāh hăwāʾ miṯnaṣṣaḥ ʿal-sārəḵayyāʾ wa-ʾăḥašdarpənayyāʾ kol-qŏḇēl dī rûaḥ yattîrāʾ bēh ū-malkāʾ ʿăšîṯ la-hăqāmūṯēh ʿal-kol-malḵūṯāʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:4 (= English 6:3; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then this Daniel became distinguished above all the other presidents and satraps, because an excellent spirit was in him; and the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom.** Joseph-pattern (Gen 39:4) + Esther-pattern (Esth 2:9) of the exile-Jew rising to imperial prominence.

verses.text: אֱדַ֨יִן סָֽרְכַיָּ֜א וַאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֗א הֲו֨וֹ בָעַ֧יִן עִלָּ֛ה לְהַשְׁכָּחָ֥ה לְדָנִיֵּ֖אל מִצַּ֣ד מַלְכוּתָ֑א וְכָל־עִלָּ֨ה וּשְׁחִיתָ֜ה לָא־יָכְלִ֣ין לְהַשְׁכָּחָ֗ה כָּל־קֳבֵל֙ דִּֽי־מְהֵימַ֣ן ה֔וּא וְכָל־שָׁלוּ֙ וּשְׁחִיתָ֔ה לָ֥א הִשְׁתְּכַ֖חַת עֲלֽוֹהִי׃
verses.translit: ʾĕdayin sārəḵayyāʾ wa-ʾăḥašdarpənayyāʾ hăwō ḇāʿayin ʿillāh lə-haškāḥāh lə-Dāniyyēʾl miṣṣaḏ malḵūṯāʾ wə-ḵol-ʿillāh ū-šəḥîṯāh lāʾ-yāḵəlîn lə-haškāḥāh kol-qŏḇēl dî-məhêman hūʾ wə-ḵol-šālū ū-šəḥîṯāh lāʾ hištəḵaḥaṯ ʿălōhî
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:5 (= English 6:4; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then the presidents and satraps sought to find a ground for complaint against Daniel with regard to the kingdom; but they could find no ground for complaint or fault, because he was faithful, and no error or fault was found in him.** **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Luke 23:4, 23:14, 23:22 (Pilate finds no fault in Jesus); cf. John 18:38, 19:4, 19:6. The Lucan-Johannine 'no fault in him' formula explicitly inherits Dan 6:5 — Daniel-Jesus typology, foundational for early Christological reading.

verses.text: אֱ֠דַיִן גֻּבְרַיָּ֤א אִלֵּךְ֙ אָֽמְרִ֔ין דִּ֣י לָ֧א נְהַשְׁכַּ֛ח לְדָנִיֵּ֥אל דְּנָ֖ה כָּל־עִלָּ֑ה לָהֵ֕ן הַשְׁכַּ֥חְנָֽה עֲל֖וֹהִי בְּדָ֥ת אֱלָהֵֽהּ׃
verses.translit: ʾĕdayin guḇrayyāʾ ʾillēḵ ʾāmərîn dī lāʾ nəhaškaḥ lə-Dāniyyēʾl dənāh kol-ʿillāh lāhēn haškaḥnāh ʿălōhî bə-ḏāṯ ʾĕlāhēh
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:6 (= English 6:5; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then these men said: 'We shall not find any ground for complaint against this Daniel unless we find it in connection with the law of his God.'** **THE CONSPIRACY'S RECOGNITION**: the only vulnerability is religious observance. The pattern of religiously-loyal Jew vs imperial-pressure is the foundational martyrdom-narrative structure. Qere-ketiv: כנמא/like-this-pattern omitted from this verse.

verses.text: אֱ֠דַיִן סָרְכַיָּ֤א וַאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּא֙ אִלֵּ֔ן הַרְגִּ֖שׁוּ עַל־מַלְכָּ֑א וְכֵן֙ אָמְרִ֣ין לֵ֔הּ דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֖א לְעָלְמִ֥ין חֱיִֽי׃
verses.translit: ʾĕdayin sārəḵayyāʾ wa-ʾăḥašdarpənayyāʾ ʾillēn hargišū ʿal-malkāʾ wə-ḵēn ʾāmərîn lēh Dāryāweš malkāʾ lə-ʿāləmîn ḥĕyî
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:7 (= English 6:6; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then these presidents and satraps came by agreement to the king, and said to him: 'O King Darius, live forever!'**

verses.text: אִתְיָעַ֜טוּ כֹּ֣ל ׀ סָרְכֵ֣י מַלְכוּתָ֗א סִגְנַיָּ֤א וַֽאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּא֙ הַדָּֽבְרַיָּ֣א וּפַחֲוָתָ֔א לְקַיָּמָ֤ה קְיָם֙ מַלְכָּ֔א וּלְתַקָּפָ֖ה אֱסָ֑ר דִּ֣י כָל־דִּֽי־יִבְעֵ֣ה בָ֠עוּ מִן־כָּל־אֱלָ֨הּ וֶֽאֱנָ֜שׁ עַד־יוֹמִ֣ין תְּלָתִ֗ין לָהֵן֙ מִנָּ֣ךְ מַלְכָּ֔א יִתְרְמֵ֕א לְגֹ֖ב אַרְיָוָתָֽא׃
verses.translit: ʾiṯyāʿaṭū kōl sārəḵê malḵūṯāʾ siḡnayyāʾ wa-ʾăḥašdarpənayyāʾ haddāḇərayyāʾ ū-p̄aḥăwāṯāʾ lə-qayyāmāh qəyām malkāʾ ū-lə-ṯaqqāp̄āh ʾĕsār dī ḵol-dî-yiḇʿēh ḇāʿū min-kol-ʾĕlāh we-ʾĕnāš ʿaḏ-yōmîn təlāṯîn lāhēn minnāḵ malkāʾ yiṯrəmēʾ lə-ḡōḇ ʾaryāwāṯāʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:8 (= English 6:7; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'All the presidents of the kingdom, the prefects and satraps, the counselors and governors, have consulted together to establish a royal statute and to enforce an interdict, that whoever makes petition to any god or man for thirty days, except to you, O king, shall be cast into the den of lions.'** **THE THIRTY-DAY PRAYER-PROHIBITION**: an unprecedented decree elevating the king to sole-recipient-of-petition. **HISTORICAL NOTE**: no Persian-period royal edict of this type is attested; the narrative trope is the king-as-divine-claimant which would later be repeated under Antiochus IV (cf. ch 11; 1 Macc 1:54-64) and Caligula. **TERM**: גֹּב אַרְיָוָתָא (gōḇ ʾaryāwāṯāʾ 'den/pit of lions') — Persian royal lion-pit attested in iconography. Cross-corpus to 6:6-9 conspiracy decree: Persian-period martyrology.

verses.text: כְּעַ֣ן מַלְכָּ֔א תְּקִ֥ים אֱסָרָ֖א וְתִרְשֻׁ֣ם כְּתָבָ֑א דִּ֣י לָ֧א לְהַשְׁנָיָ֛ה כְּדָת־מָדַ֥י וּפָרַ֖ס דִּי־לָ֥א תֶעְדֵּֽא׃
verses.translit: kəʿan malkāʾ təqîm ʾĕsārāʾ wə-ṯiršum kəṯāḇāʾ dī lāʾ lə-hašnāyāh kə-ḏāṯ-Māḏay ū-P̄ārās dî-lāʾ ṯeʿdēʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:9 (= English 6:8; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'Now, O king, establish the interdict and sign the document, so that it cannot be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be revoked.'** **THE IRREVOCABILITY TROPE**: 'law of the Medes and Persians which cannot be revoked' — appears here, v 12, v 15, and Esth 1:19, 8:8. Historically, Persian royal decrees were NOT absolutely irrevocable; the trope is Hellenistic-period literary commonplace mocking Persian-imperial rigidity.

verses.text: כָּל־קֳבֵ֖ל דְּנָ֑ה מַלְכָּא֙ דָּרְיָ֔וֶשׁ רְשַׁ֥ם כְּתָבָ֖א וֶאֱסָרָֽא׃
verses.translit: kol-qŏḇēl dənāh malkāʾ Dāryāweš rəšam kəṯāḇāʾ we-ʾĕsārāʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:10 (= English 6:9; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Therefore King Darius signed the document and interdict.**

verses.text: וְ֠דָנִיֵּאל כְּדִ֨י יְדַ֜ע דִּֽי־רְשִׁ֤ים כְּתָבָא֙ עַ֣ל לְבַיְתֵ֔הּ וְכַוִּ֨ין פְּתִיחָ֥ן לֵהּ֙ בְּעִלִּיתֵ֔הּ נֶ֖גֶד יְרוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וְזִמְנִין֩ תְּלָתָ֨ה בְיוֹמָ֜א ה֣וּא ׀ בָּרֵ֣ךְ עַל־בִּרְכ֗וֹהִי וּמְצַלֵּ֤א וּמוֹדֵא֙ קֳדָ֣ם אֱלָהֵ֔הּ כָּל־קֳבֵל֙ דִּֽי־הֲוָ֣א עָבֵ֔ד מִן־קַדְמַ֖ת דְּנָֽה׃
verses.translit: wə-Dāniyyēʾl kə-ḏî yəḏaʿ dî-rəšîm kəṯāḇāʾ ʿal lə-ḇaytēh wə-ḵawwîn pəṯîḥān lēh bə-ʿillîṯēh neḡeḏ Yərūšəlem wə-zimnîn təlāṯāh ḇə-yōmāʾ hūʾ bārēḵ ʿal-birkōhî ū-məṣallēʾ ū-mōḏēʾ qŏdām ʾĕlāhēh kol-qŏḇēl dî-hăwāʾ ʿāḇēḏ min-qaḏmaṯ dənāh
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:11 (= English 6:10; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **When Daniel knew that the document had been signed, he went to his house — where he had windows in his upper chamber open toward Jerusalem — and got down upon his knees three times a day and prayed and gave thanks before his God, as he had done previously.** **DAILY PRAYER-PRAXIS**: three-times daily (morning, midday, evening per Ps 55:17) — foundational for the Jewish Shacharit/Mincha/Maariv hours and the Christian canonical hours. Praying toward Jerusalem: cf. 1 Kgs 8:48 (Solomon's temple-dedication prayer); cf. m. Berakhot 4:5-6 — the Mishnah's prayer-direction halakha; the precedent for Mecca-orientation in Islam. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Acts 10:9, 3:1 (Peter's prayer-hours); cf. Didache 8:3 (three daily prayers).

verses.text: אֱ֠דַיִן גֻּבְרַיָּ֤א אִלֵּךְ֙ הַרְגִּ֔שׁוּ וְהַשְׁכַּ֖חוּ לְדָנִיֵּ֑אל בָּעֵ֥א וּמִתְחַנַּ֖ן קֳדָ֥ם אֱלָהֵֽהּ׃
verses.translit: ʾĕdayin guḇrayyāʾ ʾillēḵ hargišū wə-haškaḥū lə-Dāniyyēʾl bāʿēʾ ū-miṯḥannan qŏdām ʾĕlāhēh
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:12 (= English 6:11; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then these men came by agreement and found Daniel making petition and supplication before his God.**

verses.text: בֵּ֠אדַיִן קְרִ֨יבוּ וְאָמְרִ֥ין קֳדָם־מַלְכָּא֮ עַל־אֱסָ֣ר מַלְכָּא֒ הֲלָ֧א אֱסָ֣ר רְשַׁ֗מְתָּ דִּ֣י כָל־אֱנָ֡שׁ דִּֽי־יִבְעֵה֩ מִן־כָּל־אֱלָ֨הּ וֶֽאֱנָ֜שׁ עַד־יוֹמִ֣ין תְּלָתִ֗ין לָהֵן֙ מִנָּ֣ךְ מַלְכָּ֔א יִתְרְמֵ֕א לְג֖וֹב אַרְיָוָתָ֑א עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֗ר יַצִּיבָ֧א מִלְּתָ֛א כְּדָת־מָדַ֥י וּפָרַ֖ס דִּי־לָ֥א תֶעְדֵּֽא׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin qərîḇū wə-ʾāmərîn qŏdām-malkāʾ ʿal-ʾĕsār malkāʾ hălāʾ ʾĕsār rəšamtā dī ḵol-ʾĕnāš dî-yiḇʿēh min-kol-ʾĕlāh we-ʾĕnāš ʿaḏ-yōmîn təlāṯîn lāhēn minnāḵ malkāʾ yiṯrəmēʾ lə-ḡōḇ ʾaryāwāṯāʾ ʿănēh malkāʾ wə-ʾāmar yaṣṣîḇāʾ milləṯāʾ kə-ḏāṯ-Māḏay ū-P̄ārās dî-lāʾ ṯeʿdēʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:13 (= English 6:12; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then they approached and said before the king, concerning the king's interdict: 'Did you not sign an interdict, that any man who makes petition to any god or man within thirty days except to you, O king, shall be cast into the den of lions?' The king answered: 'The thing stands fast, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be revoked.'**

verses.text: בֵּ֠אדַיִן עֲנ֣וֹ וְאָמְרִין֮ קֳדָ֣ם מַלְכָּא֒ דִּ֣י דָנִיֵּ֡אל דִּי֩ מִן־בְּנֵ֨י גָלוּתָ֜א דִּ֣י יְה֗וּד לָא־שָׂ֨ם עליך עֲלָ֤ךְ מַלְכָּא֙ טְעֵ֔ם וְעַל־אֱסָרָ֖א דִּ֣י רְשַׁ֑מְתָּ וְזִמְנִ֤ין תְּלָתָה֙ בְּיוֹמָ֔א בָּעֵ֖א בָּעוּתֵֽהּ׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin ʿănō wə-ʾāmərîn qŏdām malkāʾ dī Dāniyyēʾl dī min-bənê ḡālūṯāʾ dī Yəhūḏ lāʾ-śām ʿălāḵ malkāʾ ṭəʿēm wə-ʿal-ʾĕsārāʾ dī rəšamtā wə-zimnîn təlāṯāh bə-yōmāʾ bāʿēʾ bāʿūṯēh
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:14 (= English 6:13; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then they answered before the king: 'That Daniel, who is one of the exiles from Judah, pays no heed to you, O king, or the interdict you have signed, but makes his petition three times a day.'** Qere-ketiv: עליך/עֲלָךְ.

verses.text: אֱדַ֨יִן מַלְכָּ֜א כְּדִ֧י מִלְּתָ֣א שְׁמַ֗ע שַׂגִּיא֙ בְּאֵ֣שׁ עֲל֔וֹהִי וְעַ֧ל דָּנִיֵּ֛אל שָׂ֥ם בָּ֖ל לְשֵׁיזָבוּתֵ֑הּ וְעַד֙ מֶֽעָלֵ֣י שִׁמְשָׁ֔א הֲוָ֥א מִשְׁתַּדַּ֖ר לְהַצָּלוּתֵֽהּ׃
verses.translit: ʾĕdayin malkāʾ kə-ḏî milləṯāʾ šəmaʿ śaggîʾ bə-ʾēš ʿălōhî wə-ʿal Dāniyyēʾl śām bāl lə-šêzāḇūṯēh wə-ʿaḏ meʿālê šimšāʾ hăwāʾ mištaddar lə-haṣṣālūṯēh
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:15 (= English 6:14; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then the king, when he heard these words, was much distressed, and set his mind to deliver Daniel; and he labored till the going down of the sun to rescue him.** The king's reluctance contrasts with ch 3's Nebuchadnezzar's eagerness — Darius is a sympathetic-but-trapped figure.

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֙יִן֙ גֻּבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֔ךְ הַרְגִּ֖שׁוּ עַל־מַלְכָּ֑א וְאָמְרִ֣ין לְמַלְכָּ֗א דַּ֤ע מַלְכָּא֙ דִּֽי־דָת֙ לְמָדַ֣י וּפָרַ֔ס דִּֽי־כָל־אֱסָ֥ר וּקְיָ֛ם דִּֽי־מַלְכָּ֥א יְהָקֵ֖ים לָ֥א לְהַשְׁנָיָֽה׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin guḇrayyāʾ ʾillēḵ hargišū ʿal-malkāʾ wə-ʾāmərîn lə-malkāʾ daʿ malkāʾ dî-ḏāṯ lə-Māḏay ū-P̄ārās dî-ḵol-ʾĕsār ū-qəyām dî-malkāʾ yə-hāqêm lāʾ lə-hašnāyāh
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:16 (= English 6:15; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then these men came by agreement to the king, and said to the king: 'Know, O king, that it is a law of the Medes and Persians that no interdict or statute which the king establishes can be changed.'**

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֜יִן מַלְכָּ֣א אֲמַ֗ר וְהַיְתִיו֙ לְדָ֣נִיֵּ֔אל וּרְמ֕וֹ לְגֻבָּ֖א דִּ֣י אַרְיָוָתָ֑א עָנֵ֤ה מַלְכָּא֙ וְאָמַ֣ר לְדָנִיֵּ֔אל אֱלָהָ֗ךְ דִּ֣י אַנְתְּ פָּֽלַֽח־לֵ֤הּ בִּתְדִירָא֙ ה֖וּא יְשֵׁיזְבִנָּֽךְ׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin malkāʾ ʾămar wə-haytîw lə-Dāniyyēʾl ū-rəmō lə-ḡubbāʾ dī ʾaryāwāṯāʾ ʿănēh malkāʾ wə-ʾāmar lə-Dāniyyēʾl ʾĕlāhāḵ dī ʾant pālaḥ-lēh bi-ṯḏîrāʾ hūʾ yəšêzəḇinnāḵ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:17 (= English 6:16; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then the king commanded, and Daniel was brought and cast into the den of lions. The king said to Daniel: 'May your God, whom you serve continually, deliver you!'** The king's blessing-prayer is functionally identical to Nebuchadnezzar's recognition of YHWH in 3:28.

verses.text: וְהֵיתָ֙יִת֙ אֶ֣בֶן חֲדָ֔ה וְשֻׂמַ֖ת עַל־פֻּ֣ם גֻּבָּ֑א וְחַתְמַ֨הּ מַלְכָּ֜א בְּעִזְקְתֵ֗הּ וּבְעִזְקָת֙ רַבְרְבָנ֔וֹהִי דִּ֛י לָא־תִשְׁנֵ֥א צְב֖וּ בְּדָנִיֵּֽאל׃
verses.translit: wə-hêṯāyiṯ ʾeḇen ḥăḏāh wə-śumaṯ ʿal-pum gubbāʾ wə-ḥaṯmah malkāʾ bə-ʿizqəṯēh ū-ḇə-ʿizqāṯ raḇrəḇānōhî dī lāʾ-ṯišnēʾ ṣəḇū bə-Dāniyyēʾl
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:18 (= English 6:17; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **A stone was brought and laid upon the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet and with the signet of his lords, that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel.** **THE SEALED-STONE-OVER-PIT MOTIF**: **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR**: cf. Matt 27:60, 27:66; Mark 15:46; Luke 24:2; John 20:1 (the stone sealed over Jesus' tomb). The Daniel-Christ typology is one of the most striking patristic cross-corpus readings (Tertullian, Cyprian, Origen). The death/rescue from sealed-pit narrative-shape directly underlies the Christian resurrection-narrative composition.

verses.text: אֱ֠דַיִן אֲזַ֨ל מַלְכָּ֤א לְהֵֽיכְלֵהּ֙ וּבָ֣ת טְוָ֔ת וְדַחֲוָ֖ן לָא־הַנְעֵ֣ל קָֽדָמ֑וֹהִי וְשִׁנְתֵּ֖הּ נַדַּ֥ת עֲלֽוֹהִי׃
verses.translit: ʾĕdayin ʾăzal malkāʾ lə-hêḵəlēh ū-ḇāṯ ṭəwāṯ wə-ḏaḥăwān lāʾ-hanʿēl qodāmōhî wə-šintēh naddaṯ ʿălōhî
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:19 (= English 6:18; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then the king went to his palace and spent the night fasting; no diversions were brought to him, and sleep fled from him.** Royal-vigil for the condemned righteous man.

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֣יִן מַלְכָּ֔א בִּשְׁפַּרְפָּרָ֖א יְק֣וּם בְּנָגְהָ֑א וּבְהִ֨תְבְּהָלָ֔ה לְגֻבָּ֥א דִֽי־אַרְיָוָתָ֖א אֲזַֽל׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin malkāʾ bi-špar-pārāʾ yəqūm bə-nāḡəhāʾ ū-ḇə-hiṯbəhālāh lə-ḡubbāʾ ḏî-ʾaryāwāṯāʾ ʾăzal
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:20 (= English 6:19; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then, at break of day, the king arose and went in haste to the den of lions.** Dawn-visit-to-the-sealed-pit. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Mark 16:2 ('very early on the first day of the week... when the sun had risen'); Matt 28:1; Luke 24:1; John 20:1 — the women come to the tomb at dawn. The Dan 6:20 dawn-visit-to-the-tomb narrative-arc is foundational for the Easter morning composition.

verses.text: וּכְמִקְרְבֵ֣הּ לְגֻבָּ֔א לְדָ֣נִיֵּ֔אל בְּקָ֥ל עֲצִ֖יב זְעִ֑ק עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֣ר לְדָנִיֵּ֗אל דָּֽנִיֵּאל֙ עֲבֵד֙ אֱלָהָ֣א חַיָּ֔א אֱלָהָ֗ךְ דִּ֣י אַנְתְּ פָּֽלַֽח־לֵ֤הּ בִּתְדִירָא֙ הַיְכִ֣ל לְשֵׁיזָבוּתָ֔ךְ מִן־אַרְיָוָתָֽא׃
verses.translit: ū-ḵə-miqrəḇēh lə-ḡubbāʾ lə-Dāniyyēʾl bə-qāl ʿăṣîḇ zəʿiq ʿănēh malkāʾ wə-ʾāmar lə-Dāniyyēʾl Dāniyyēʾl ʿăḇēḏ ʾĕlāhāʾ ḥayyāʾ ʾĕlāhāḵ dī ʾant pālaḥ-lēh bi-ṯḏîrāʾ hayḵîl lə-šêzāḇūṯāḵ min-ʾaryāwāṯāʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:21 (= English 6:20; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **When he came near to the den, he cried out to Daniel in a tone of anguish; the king said to Daniel: 'O Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God whom you serve continually been able to deliver you from the lions?'** **TITLE**: אֱלָהָא חַיָּא (ʾĕlāhāʾ ḥayyāʾ 'the living God') — appears here and v 26 in Aramaic Daniel. **CROSS-CORPUS**: Hebrew אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים cf. Deut 5:26; Josh 3:10; 1 Sam 17:26; Jer 10:10; Matt 16:16 (Peter's confession: 'Christ, the Son of the living God'); 1 Tim 3:15; Heb 10:31; Rev 7:2.

verses.text: אֱדַ֙יִן֙ דָּנִיֶּ֔אל עִם־מַלְכָּ֖א מַלִּ֑ל מַלְכָּ֖א לְעָלְמִ֥ין חֱיִֽי׃
verses.translit: ʾĕdayin Dāniyyel ʿim-malkāʾ mallil malkāʾ lə-ʿāləmîn ḥĕyî
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:22 (= English 6:21; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then Daniel said to the king: 'O king, live forever!'**

verses.text: אֱלָהִ֞י שְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאֲכֵ֗הּ וּֽסֲגַ֛ר פֻּ֥ם אַרְיָוָתָ֖א וְלָ֣א חַבְּל֑וּנִי כָּל־קֳבֵ֗ל דִּ֤י קָֽדָמ֙וֹהִי֙ זָכוּ֙ הִשְׁתְּכַ֣חַת לִ֔י וְאַ֤ף קדמיך קָֽדָמָךְ֙ מַלְכָּ֔א חֲבוּלָ֖ה לָ֥א עַבְדֵֽת׃
verses.translit: ʾĕlāhî šəlaḥ malʾăḵēh ū-səḡar pum ʾaryāwāṯāʾ wə-lāʾ ḥabbəlūnî kol-qŏḇēl dī qodāmōhî zāḵū hištəḵaḥaṯ lî wə-ʾap̄ qodāmāḵ malkāʾ ḥăḇūlāh lāʾ ʿaḇḏēṯ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:23 (= English 6:22; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'My God sent his angel and shut the lions' mouths, and they have not hurt me, because I was found blameless before him; and also before you, O king, I have done no wrong.'** **THE ANGEL-RESCUE**: exact parallel to 3:28 (Nebuchadnezzar: 'his angel delivered his servants'). **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Heb 11:33 ('who through faith... stopped the mouths of lions') — explicit Dan 6:23 quotation. cf. 2 Tim 4:17 ('I was rescued from the lion's mouth'). cf. Ps 22:21. cf. 1 Pet 5:8 ('the devil prowls like a roaring lion'). Qere-ketiv: קדמיך/קָדָמָךְ.

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֣יִן מַלְכָּ֗א שַׂגִּיא֙ טְאֵ֣ב עֲל֔וֹהִי וּלְדָ֣נִיֵּ֔אל אֲמַ֖ר לְהַנְסָקָ֣ה מִן־גֻּבָּ֑א וְהֻסַּ֨ק דָּנִיֵּ֜אל מִן־גֻּבָּ֗א וְכָל־חֲבָל֙ לָא־הִשְׁתְּכַ֣ח בֵּ֔הּ דִּ֖י הֵימִ֥ן בֵּאלָהֵֽהּ׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin malkāʾ śaggîʾ ṭəʾēḇ ʿălōhî ū-lə-Dāniyyēʾl ʾămar lə-hansāqāh min-gubbāʾ wə-hussaq Dāniyyēʾl min-gubbāʾ wə-ḵol-ḥăḇāl lāʾ-hištəḵaḥ bēh dī hêmin bê-ʾlāhēh
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:24 (= English 6:23; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then the king was exceedingly glad, and commanded that Daniel be taken up out of the den; and Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no kind of hurt was found upon him, because he had trusted in his God.** Parallel to 3:27 ('no kind of injury was found on them').

verses.text: וַאֲמַ֣ר מַלְכָּ֡א וְהַיְתִ֡יו גֻּבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּךְ֩ דִּֽי־אֲכַ֨לוּ קַרְצ֜וֹהִי דִּ֣י דָֽנִיֵּ֗אל וּלְגֹ֤ב אַרְיָוָתָא֙ רְמ֔וֹ אִנּ֖וּן בְּנֵיה֣וֹן וּנְשֵׁיה֑וֹן וְלָֽא־מְט֞וֹ לְאַרְעִ֣ית גֻּבָּ֗א עַ֠ד דִּֽי־שְׁלִ֤טֽוּ בְהוֹן֙ אַרְיָוָ֣תָ֔א וְכָל־גַּרְמֵיה֖וֹן הַדִּֽקוּ׃
verses.translit: wa-ʾămar malkāʾ wə-haytîw guḇrayyāʾ ʾillēḵ dî-ʾăḵalū qarṣōhî dî Dāniyyēʾl ū-lə-ḡōḇ ʾaryāwāṯāʾ rəmō ʾinnūn bənêhōn ū-nəšêhōn wə-lāʾ-məṭō lə-ʾarʿîṯ gubbāʾ ʿaḏ dî-šəliṭū ḇə-hōn ʾaryāwāṯāʾ wə-ḵol-garmêhōn haddiqū
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:25 (= English 6:24; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **The king commanded, and the men who had accused Daniel were brought and cast into the den of lions — they, their children, and their wives; and before they reached the bottom of the den, the lions overpowered them and broke all their bones to pieces.** **POETIC-JUSTICE EXECUTION** — accusers receive the punishment they sought. Wives + children share the punishment (collective-punishment trope; cf. Esth 9 the execution of Haman's sons; cf. Num 16 the swallowing of Korah's families).

verses.text: בֵּאדַ֣יִן דָּרְיָ֣וֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֡א כְּ֠תַב לְֽכָל־עַֽמְמַיָּ֞א אֻמַּיָּ֧א וְלִשָּׁנַיָּ֛א דִּֽי־דארין דָיְרִ֥ין בְּכָל־אַרְעָ֖א שְׁלָמְכ֥וֹן יִשְׂגֵּֽא׃
verses.translit: bēʾḏayin Dāryāweš malkāʾ kəṯaḇ lə-ḵol-ʿammə-mayyāʾ ʾummayyāʾ wə-liššānayyāʾ dî-ḏāyərîn bə-ḵol-ʾarʿāʾ šəlāməḵōn yiśgēʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:26 (= English 6:25; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **Then King Darius wrote to all peoples, nations, and languages that dwell in all the earth: 'Peace be multiplied to you!'** Encyclical-letter framing parallels 4:1. Tripartite formula 'peoples, nations, languages' repeats. Qere-ketiv: דארין/דָיְרִין.

verses.text: מִן־קֳדָמַי֮ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵם֒ דִּ֣י ׀ בְּכָל־שָׁלְטָ֣ן מַלְכוּתִ֗י לֶהֱוֺ֤ן זאעין זָיְעִין֙ וְדָ֣חֲלִ֔ין מִן־קֳדָ֖ם אֱלָהֵ֣הּ דִּי־דָֽנִיֵּ֑אל דִּי־ה֣וּא ׀ אֱלָהָ֣א חַיָּ֗א וְקַיָּם֙ לְעָ֣לְמִ֔ין וּמַלְכוּתֵהּ֙ דִּֽי־לָ֣א תִתְחַבַּ֔ל וְשָׁלְטָנֵ֖הּ עַד־סוֹפָֽא׃
verses.translit: min-qodāmay śîm ṭəʿēm dī bə-ḵol-šolṭān malḵūṯî lehĕwōn zāyəʿîn wə-ḏāḥălîn min-qodām ʾĕlāhēh dî-Dāniyyēʾl dî-hūʾ ʾĕlāhāʾ ḥayyāʾ wə-qayyām lə-ʿāləmîn ū-malḵūṯēh dî-lāʾ ṯiṯḥabbal wə-šolṭānēh ʿaḏ-sōp̄āʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:27 (= English 6:26; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'I make a decree, that in all my royal dominion men should tremble and fear before the God of Daniel, for he is the living God, enduring forever; his kingdom shall never be destroyed, and his dominion shall be to the end.'** **THE EVERLASTING-KINGDOM REFRAIN** repeats (cf. 4:3, 4:34, 7:14, 7:27). Title 'living God enduring forever' (אֱלָהָא חַיָּא וְקַיָּם לְעָלְמִין). **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Rev 11:15 ('the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord... and he shall reign forever and ever'); cf. Luke 1:33 ('of his kingdom there shall be no end'). Qere-ketiv: זאעין/זָיְעִין.

verses.text: מְשֵׁיזִ֣ב וּמַצִּ֗ל וְעָבֵד֙ אָתִ֣ין וְתִמְהִ֔ין בִּשְׁמַיָּ֖א וּבְאַרְעָ֑א דִּ֚י שֵׁיזִ֣יב לְדָֽנִיֵּ֔אל מִן־יַ֖ד אַרְיָוָתָֽא׃
verses.translit: məšêziḇ ū-maṣṣil wə-ʿāḇēḏ ʾāṯîn wə-ṯimhîn bi-šmayyāʾ ū-ḇə-ʾarʿāʾ dī šêziḇ lə-Dāniyyēʾl min-yaḏ ʾaryāwāṯāʾ
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:28 (= English 6:27; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **'He delivers and rescues; he works signs and wonders in heaven and on earth; he who has saved Daniel from the power of the lions.'** Echoes 4:3 + 4:34. End of the imperial-decree.

verses.text: וְדָנִיֵּ֣אל דְּנָ֔ה הַצְלַ֖ח בְּמַלְכ֣וּת דָּרְיָ֑וֶשׁ וּבְמַלְכ֖וּת כּ֥וֹרֶשׁ פרסיא פָּרְסָאָֽה׃
verses.translit: wə-Dāniyyēʾl dənāh haṣlaḥ bə-malḵūṯ Dāryāweš ū-ḇə-malḵūṯ Kōreš Pārəsāʾāh
verses.witness_primary: BHS Codex Leningradensis Dan 6:29 (= English 6:28; Aramaic)
verses.notes: **So this Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus the Persian.** **CHAPTER-CLOSING TRANSITION**: bridges the court-tales (chs 1-6) to the apocalyptic visions (chs 7-12). Daniel's lifespan as a courtier spans the Babylonian, Median, and Persian periods — establishing his prophetic authority across the four-kingdom sequence. **NOTE ON CYRUS**: כּוֹרֶשׁ פָּרְסָאָה (Kōreš Pārəsāʾāh 'Cyrus the Persian') — historically Cyrus II, founder of the Achaemenid empire, took Babylon 539 BCE. Qere-ketiv: פרסיא/פָּרְסָאָה.
